text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today as oil prices declined, with US crude dropping to $89.62 per barrel. Despite ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—including Iranian military strikes on U.S. bases in Kuwait and threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz—the actual price of oil moved lower, which directly weighs on an oil producer's near-term returns. The stock had climbed sharply over the prior three days (from $137.86 to $142.28) likely on initial concerns those tensions would tighten supply; today's pullback reflects a reassessment that the market isn't pricing in an immediate shortage.

The broader pattern here is a tension between geopolitical risk and actual crude supply. Even with military escalation and warnings that the Hormuz corridor is no longer seen as reliably safe, global oil is trading in the low $90s rather than spiking—suggesting markets may not yet believe disruptions will materially reduce flows. For an oil producer, that means the upside from conflict-driven scarcity isn't materializing as prices stabilize.
